questions.prompt: What did Europeans of the 1700s call placing smallpox scabs under the skin?
questions.explanation: Jenner later replaced smallpox scabs with cowpox.

questions.prompt: What made Jenner's method safer than variolation?

options.text: He used antibodies taken from smallpox survivors
He used a synthetic arsenic-based drug
He used inactivated smallpox from old scabs
He used cowpox, a related but milder virus

questions.explanation: Milkmaids with cowpox rarely got smallpox.

questions.prompt: The word 'vaccine' comes from vacca, Latin for:
questions.explanation: Pasteur coined it in honor of Jenner's cowpox work.

questions.prompt: Why can't you get the flu from a flu shot?

options.text: It contains only antibodies, not any virus parts
It contains only a toxoid made from flu toxin
The virus in it is inactivated and can't reproduce
It's an mRNA vaccine with no viral proteins

questions.explanation: Flu-like symptoms are your immune response.

questions.prompt: In an mRNA COVID vaccine, what do your cells produce from the mRNA?
questions.explanation: Displayed spike fragments trigger an active immune response.

questions.prompt: Why must mRNA vaccines be stored at extremely cold temperatures?

options.text: RNA is unstable and breaks down quickly

questions.prompt: How does the DNA COVID vaccine get its DNA into the nucleus?

options.text: Lipid nanoparticles fuse with the nucleus
An inactivated adenoviral vector carries it
It is injected directly into nuclei

questions.explanation: Then it's transcribed into spike mRNA.

questions.prompt: Paul Ehrlich's 'magic bullet' idea was to:

options.text: Attach a toxic drug to a dye that seeks a target
Use mold growing on plates to kill bacteria
Use bacteriophages to destroy specific bacteria
Spray germicides like carbolic acid over wounds

questions.explanation: Preparation 606 = arsenic attached to a dye.
Ehrlich thought spirochetes looked like trypanosomes.

questions.prompt: Which antibiotic works by inhibiting protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: It targets the 70S ribosome; streptomycin and erythromycin do too.

questions.prompt: A patient has a known strep infection. Which choice is generally better, and why?

options.text: No drug — strep can't be treated
A broad-spectrum drug, to kill everything
A narrow-spectrum drug, to spare the normal flora

questions.explanation: Broad-spectrum drugs are for unknown pathogens.

questions.prompt: Which is an advantage of phage therapy over antibiotics?

options.text: It works without knowing the pathogen
It kills every kind of bacteria
It is highly specific and self-amplifying

questions.explanation: It also self-eliminates once the pathogen is gone.

questions.prompt: Bonnie Bassler's quorum-sensing inhibitors work by:

options.text: Activating complement so the MAC bursts the bacteria
Killing the bacteria with arsenic attached to a dye
Breaking down the bacteria's peptidoglycan cell walls
Blocking signal receptors so bacteria never turn toxic

questions.prompt: Name the five vaccine types and give one example of each.
questions.explanation: Attenuated whole agent (MMR, Sabin polio); inactivated whole agent (flu shot, rabies, Salk polio); subunit (hepatitis B, HPV); toxoid (tetanus, diphtheria); nucleic acid (COVID mRNA or DNA).
